title: Number of Changing Keys
summary: Given a string s typed by a user, count the number of times the user used a key different from the last used key, excluding changes due to modifiers like shift or caps lock.
statement: Given a string s typed by a user, count the number of times the user used a key different from the last used key, excluding changes due to modifiers like shift or caps lock.
constraints: Treat uppercase and lowercase forms of the same letter as the same keyboard key.
Count adjacent positions where the key changes.
Return the number of changes while reading the string left to right.
reference_solution:
def case_insensitive_key_changes(s):
    return sum(a.lower()!=b.lower() for a,b in zip(s,s[1:]))
hints: Normalize character case before comparing keys.
Compare each character with its immediate predecessor.
Add one exactly when their lowercase forms differ.
Every key transition lies between one adjacent pair, and every differing adjacent pair is one transition.
editorial: Every key transition lies between one adjacent pair, and every differing adjacent pair is one transition.

tests.explanation: Case changes alone do not count; transitions a-to-b and b-to-c give two.
Every character uses the same key, so the answer is zero.
